subject: Dedicated SLO targets — feedback + risks vs capacity realities
body:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Keiko Yamamoto <keiko.yamamoto@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 22, 2026 at 9:14 AM
Subject: Dedicated SLO targets — feedback + risks vs capacity realities

Hi Sean / Rafa,

Thanks for circulating the Dedicated SLO strawman. I’m aligned with the direction (separate tier targets + explicit enforcement), but I want to flag a few risks where the initial targets may be disconnected from how Dedicated capacity actually behaves, especially during pool scaling/provision-to-ready.

Key points:

1) Availability SLO vs “no capacity” / readiness
- Customers experience “Dedicated is down” when they get queueing/timeouts because pool readiness dips, even if the inference stack is otherwise healthy.
- If we measure pure API 2xx/5xx without a readiness/capacity signal, we’ll have a mismatch between customer pain and what the SLO captures.
- Suggest Dedicated has two first-class journeys:
  a) Inference request success rate (incl. timeouts) — per customer pool
  b) Pool readiness (capacity available + scheduler healthy) — per customer pool

2) Latency targets need to reflect warm vs cold behavior
- Our current operational reality is that some customers have traffic patterns that trigger autoscaling cold-start paths (esp. nights/weekends).
- If we set a p99 target that assumes warm steady-state 100% of the time, we’ll blow budgets frequently and effectively stay in freeze/soft-block.
- I’m supportive of tighter latency targets, but we should explicitly define whether p95/p99 is on “served requests” only, and how we treat requests delayed due to provisioning.

3) Phased enforcement is critical for Dedicated
- Dedicated customers expect isolation, but we still have shared dependencies (control plane, routing, certain regional GPU constraints).
- Recommendation:
  - Phase A: publish targets + dashboards + alerting (no gates)
  - Phase B: warn-only gates for a pilot set of services (gateway, routing, scheduler)
  - Phase C: soft-block for “feature shipping” changes; allow emergency fixes with override
  - Phase D: hard-block only once readiness SLI is stable + we’ve backtested at least a quarter

4) Targets (proposed adjustments)
I don’t want to bikeshed numbers too early, but directional feedback:
- Availability (inference success): 99.9% monthly is fine as a long-term goal, but I’d prefer we start at 99.7–99.8% while readiness SLI is maturing, then ratchet.
- Pool readiness: we should set a separate target that matches what we can actually deliver given regional capacity constraints + autoscaling lag (and be explicit about maintenance windows if any).
- Latency: I’m more comfortable with p95 targets per route/model, but p99 will be noisy until we separate TTFT vs total stream duration for streaming.

Attached are:
- Dedicated_SLO_targets_strawman_v2.xlsx — my edits / notes
- Dedicated_SLO_customer_expectations_mapping_notes.docx — quick mapping of current customer expectations (not contractual SLA language) vs proposed targets and how I think we message it.

Ask:
- Can we schedule 30 mins early next week to align on Dedicated target principles before we publish the first “canonical” table?
- Also: can someone confirm whether Dedicated SLI calculation will exclude customer-side client aborts (and how we classify “499” equivalents)? I want to avoid us accidentally counting client disconnects as Redwood failures.

Thanks,
Lauren

Lauren Bishop
Director of Product, Dedicated
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Keiko Yamamoto <keiko.yamamoto@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 22, 2026 at 10:02 AM
Subject: Re: Dedicated SLO targets — feedback + risks vs capacity realities

Lauren — this is great, thank you.

Agree on splitting the journeys. We were leaning toward “request success” as the core and treating readiness as supporting telemetry, but I’m convinced it needs to be first-class for Dedicated (otherwise we’ll be fighting the customer perception gap constantly).

On phased enforcement: +1. We’re aligned that enforcement should not come before we trust the SLIs and have done backtesting.

Next steps from my side:
- Rafa/Aisha: can you propose a concrete definition for “pool readiness” that we can measure consistently (scheduler health + capacity signal), and how it maps to paging vs ticket-only?
- I’ll ask Sergio to validate whether we can build per-customer readiness views without creating a metrics/cardinality explosion.

Re: client aborts (499): we should exclude customer-side aborts from availability SLI; the tricky part is streaming and intermediate disconnects (TTFT vs mid-stream). Aisha has been collecting edge cases.

Let’s do 30 mins next week. I’ll have my EA send options.

Sean

Sean Gallagher
Director, Site Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Keiko Yamamoto <keiko.yamamoto@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 22, 2026 at 11:17 AM
Subject: Re: Dedicated SLO targets — feedback + risks vs capacity realities

+1 to all of this.

A few clarifications / proposals:

1) What counts as an “availability” failure for Dedicated
- 5xx (gateway/routing/runtime)
- 408/timeout where we can attribute to Redwood (queueing beyond threshold, upstream timeouts from internal hops)
- “No capacity” responses if we explicitly return them (we should treat as failures for Dedicated unless within an agreed exception window)

2) Readiness SLI definition (draft)
We can define readiness as:
- scheduler_health == OK
- AND available_capacity_tokens_per_sec > 0 (or “available replicas > 0” depending on how we model)
- evaluated per pool, per region

This isn’t perfect, but it’s measurable and aligns with the customer experience when they hit provisioning lag.

3) Enforcement sequencing
We can align enforcement mode to budget state:
- healthy: normal deploys
- at risk: canary-only + added approver
- exhausted: freeze feature deploys; allow only mitigations/rollbacks

But I want to emphasize: we should start with WARN-ONLY across Dedicated for at least one full measurement window. Otherwise we will block ourselves during the instrumentation churn.

Lauren, can you share 1–2 concrete customer examples (even anonymized) where “readiness dip” was the core issue vs “inference errors”? It’ll help us validate the readiness signal definition.

Rafa

Rafael Mendes
SRE Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Bello <aisha.bello@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, Jan 22, 2026 at 1:36 PM
Subject: Re: Dedicated SLO targets — feedback + risks vs capacity realities

Adding some detail on disconnects / 499 / streaming since it intersects with latency targets.

For Dedicated inference success SLI, my current draft is:
- Count as SUCCESS:
  - non-streaming: HTTP 2xx
  - streaming: HTTP 2xx AND we successfully emit at least one token (TTFT achieved)
- Count as FAILURE:
  - 5xx
  - gateway-side timeouts
  - internal upstream timeouts (routing -> runtime)
  - streaming disconnects where we have evidence of server-side termination BEFORE first token
- Exclude:
  - invalid auth / invalid request
  - customer/client abort after first token (classify separately as “client_abort_mid_stream”)

This keeps “availability” aligned with “can the customer get a response started.”

For latency:
- Streaming needs two SLIs:
  1) TTFT p95/p99
  2) tokens/sec or “stream health” (but this is not a latency SLI per se)
- If we use end-to-end stream duration, the distribution is dominated by customer prompt length + stop conditions.

Vanessa: I’ll sync with you on the readiness signal; I suspect we need an explicit “provisioning” state we can tag so we can separate cold-start-induced queueing from true degradation.

Aisha

Aisha Bello
Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, Jan 22, 2026 at 3:09 PM
Subject: Re: Dedicated SLO targets — feedback + risks vs capacity realities

This thread is exactly the kind of cross-functional alignment we need.

Two platform constraints to keep in mind as we set Dedicated targets:

1) Regional GPU scarcity & maintenance events
Even for Dedicated pools, there are occasional events where capacity is constrained regionally (hardware failures, cloud capacity, etc.). We should be explicit in definitions about what is in vs out of scope for the SLO calculation (and we should have a playbook for how we mitigate).

2) Autoscaling lag is real; we need to decide whether it is “part of the product”
My bias: for Dedicated, autoscaling lag is part of the product experience and should be captured (readiness/timeout failures). That will force us to invest in faster scale-up and better prewarming.

On enforcement:
- I support warn-only first, then soft-block, then hard-block for a small set of services.
- We should define an exception path (time-bounded override) early so teams don’t route around the process ad hoc.

Lauren: if we start at 99.7–99.8% for Dedicated inference success while we mature readiness, I’m OK with that as long as we have a clear ratchet plan and we are transparent internally that it is a stepping stone.

Priya

Priya Natarajan
VP Engineering, Platform
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, Jan 23, 2026 at 11:02 AM
Subject: Re: Dedicated SLO targets — feedback + risks vs capacity realities

Thanks all — this is landing well.

Rafa: customer examples (anonymized):
1) “Fintech-1” (us-east, Llama-variant) — low baseline QPS with intermittent spikes. During spikes, pool scaled but provisioning lag caused queueing -> timeouts; customer described it as an outage. Once warm, success/latency were fine.
2) “SaaS-2” (eu-west) — readiness dipped during a scheduler issue; inference errors were low but they saw elevated p99 and occasional timeouts. Again, perceived as Dedicated being unreliable.

Aisha: your proposed classification (success = TTFT achieved for streaming) makes sense and aligns with how customers think. If we can capture “client_abort_mid_stream” separately, PM can message this better when customers show us disconnect graphs.

Priya: agree autoscaling lag should be considered part of the product experience for Dedicated. The only thing I’d like us to be careful about is not setting ourselves up for immediate enforcement-driven freeze while we improve it.

Proposal for next step:
- SRE publishes v0 Dedicated targets with explicit “ratchet plan” in the doc:
  - v0: 99.8% inference success (monthly), readiness SLI target TBD but present + tracked, latency split TTFT vs non-streaming p95
  - after backtest + 1 full window: move to 99.9% and tighten latency where data supports
- Enforcement: Dedicated stays warn-only until readiness SLI is stable and we’ve validated attribution.

If everyone’s good, I’ll update the customer expectation mapping notes to reflect the ratchet plan and provide a short paragraph CS can use when customers ask “what happens when you burn budget?” (i.e., we freeze risky changes, we prioritize mitigations, we communicate status).

Lauren
